title: Procurement Decision Canvas — Inference Platform (sketch)
body:
Slide 1 — Goal and audience:
Objective: Give field teams a single, visual canvas to guide procurement conversations for inference (hosted/dedicated/private).
Primary audiences: Procurement or vendor evaluation lead; Platform/Infra engineering; Product owner (owner of the ML feature).
Use: 10–15 minute pre-procurement brief for stakeholders + leave-behind for procurement committee.

Slide 2 — One-line positioning for procurement:
Redwood Inference reduces per-query cost and procurement risk by combining predictable reserved capacity for SLAs with a migration path to hosted burst capacity — measured in tokens, not opaque headroom buckets.
Speaker note: emphasize predictable unit economics and clearly scoped SLAs (latency percentiles, uptime, auditability).

Slide 3 — Decision criteria canvas (visual matrix):
Columns (what buyers care about): Cost predictability | Latency guarantees | Data control & compliance | Integration effort | Operational ownership | Exit/portability
Rows (how Redwood maps):
- Cost predictability: Reserved capacity + committed spend discounts, transparent per-token math, monthly reporting
- Latency guarantees: SLO-backed P99 latency tiers, regional routing, canary fallbacks to cheaper variants
- Data control: Private deployment option, VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs
- Integration effort: One API across hosted/dedicated/private, SDKs, templates, migration support (SE-led)
- Operational ownership: Redwood handles GPU infra and runtime; customer controls model pins, rollout policies
- Exit/portability: Model version pinning and exportable configs for on-prem handoff

Slide 4 — Scoring rubric for procurement committee (sample):
Ask procurement to rate each column 1–5 (1=low importance, 5=must-have). Multiply weights by Redwood fit score (0–5) to generate a procurement fit number.
Sample weights: Cost predictability=5, Latency=4, Data control=5, Integration=3, Ops=3, Exit=2.
Speaker note: This creates a defensible, documented recommendation for vendor selection.

Slide 5 — Negotiation levers (what sales can offer):
- Pricing: pilot credit, tiered committed spend discounts, volume-based price caps for embeddings
- Capacity terms: reserved GPU pool with burst windows, guaranteed baseline throughput (tokens/sec)
- SLA: P99 latency target, uptime SLA, service credits scoped to route/model
- Compliance: add-on for SOC2/ISO evidence, on-prem install support, dedicated audit logs retention
- Onboarding: 2-week SE-led integration package, response runbook and playbooks

Slide 6 — Cost example (procurement-friendly framing):
Scenario: 10M tokens/mo steady, 20% monthly burst to 15M.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): straightforward per-token rate, higher peak cost during bursts.
- Reserved (dedicated): commit to baseline 10M tokens (discount 30%), burst charge at lower cap; predictable monthly invoice and cost per 1k tokens.
Table (sample numbers):
- Hosted blended rate: $0.0018 per token -> $18,000/mo at 10M
- Reserved baseline: effective $0.0013 per token with commit -> $13,000/mo, burst cap $0.0015 for overflow
Speaker note: emphasize how committed spend reduces budget variance and simplifies procurement approvals. Numbers are illustrative; always run customer workload through cost model template.

Slide 7 — Common procurement objections + recommended responses:
Objection: "We can host ourselves cheaper."
Response: Compare TCO including engineering ops, capacity waste, SLA reliability, and development time-to-market. Provide TCO worksheet.
Objection: "How do we avoid vendor lock-in?"
Response: Show model/version pins, exportable config, on-prem private deployment option, data ingress/egress commitments.
Objection: "What about unexpected usage spikes?"
Response: Explain burst capacity model, autoscaling policies, and overage protections with spend alerts and hard caps.

Slide 8 — Procurement-ready artifacts to attach to RFP:
- Technical appendix: SLO table, latency percentiles by model family and region
- Pricing appendix: reserved vs hosted price sheet, sample scenarios
- Security/compliance bundle: SOC2/ISO, data flow diagrams, KMS/HSM integration notes
- Onboarding plan: 30/60/90 day milestones, success criteria, named SE and AM contacts

Slide 9 — Quick checklist for AE/SE before sending to procurement:
- Completed cost model with customer sample prompts and token profiles (Y/N)
- Confirmed required compliance artifacts and any gap (Y/N)
- Setup pilot environment and sample latency runbook (Y/N)
- Drafted contract terms: commit level, SLA tier, audit requirements (Y/N)

Slide 10 — Example procurement email template (short):
Subject: Redwood Inference — procurement packet and pilot proposal
Hi <Procurement Lead>,
Following our intake, attached is a compact procurement packet: pricing appendix (reserved vs hosted scenarios), SLO table, and onboarding plan. We propose a 90-day pilot with a baseline commit of X tokens/month and a capped burst window. Happy to set a 30-minute review with your legal/finance team this week.
Best,
<AE name>

Slide 11 — Next steps and owner assignments (sales play):
- AE: Confirm committed scenario and obtain PO template (owner: AE)
- SE: Run pilot with sample workload, collect latency and cost telemetry (owner: SE)
- Legal/Procurement: Review contract redlines focusing on SLA scope and audit rights (owner: Legal)
- Customer: Define success criteria (latency, cost variance, feature throughput)

Appendix — Fields team hints and scripts:
- Quick ask for customers to produce: 7–10 representative prompts, weekly token distribution, desired P99 latency target
- Quick SE script to demo procurement deck: 8–10 minute walkthrough calling out the decision canvas, then 10–15 minute Q&A on pricing and SLAs

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Need a short one-page PDF leave-behind with the scoring rubric and pricing appendix for procurement committees.
- Add two sample customer case studies: a fintech with strict latency SLAs and an enterprise with private deployment requirements.
- Tie to play: include JIRA ticket for 90-day pilot contract template and legal FAQ.
